title: AI delivers ‘zero financial payoff’ to most companies, Apollo economist says
slides: Is AI delivering zero payoff for most companies?
Apollo economist Torsten Sløk claims exactly that.
Only a few firms see financial gains from AI.
If your company isn't already measuring AI returns, start now.
Define one metric before your next AI investment.
thread_text:
1. The AI payoff illusion

Apollo economist Torsten Sløk says most companies are seeing zero return on their AI investments. Only a handful are actually making money from it.

2. A few winners, many losers

The gap is widening: companies that measure AI returns are pulling ahead, while those that don't are burning cash with no idea if it's working.

3. The measurement blind spot

Most firms never defined what success looks like before deploying AI. Without a metric, you can't tell if you're winning or just spending.

4. Start measuring now

If you haven't already set up return metrics for your AI projects, you're already behind. The first step is picking one number that matters.

5. One metric before you spend

Before your next AI investment, define a single metric you'll track. If you can't name it today, you're not ready to buy.

instagram.caption:
Most companies are getting zero financial return from AI. Not a small return — zero, according to Apollo economist Torsten Sløk.

Only a handful of firms are actually making money from it.

The gap comes down to measurement: companies tracking AI returns are pulling ahead, the rest are burning cash with no idea if it works.

If you create or publish content with AI tools, define one metric before your next investment — cost per piece, hours saved, conversion rate. Pick one.

Can you name the number you're tracking right now? 📊
